Bialystok Jewish Ghetto Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Białystok, Poland

Demolished. This cemetery was founded in 1941 to meet the needs of the Białystok Ghetto, located about 850 meters southwest of the city center within the ghetto's western section; it served as a burial site for execution victims, with about 5,000 people buried in mass graves. After the war, the site was expanded and walled, continuing to serve the Białystok Jewish community for burials, including reburials of bodies exhumed from across the city — among them those who fought in the Białystok Ghetto Uprising. Surviving Jews erected a Holocaust memorial in 1945, a memorial to the ghetto fighters in 1946, and a larger combined monument in 1948. The local government closed the cemetery in 1964, and it was fully shut down in 1971; at closure, it held over 3,500 tombstones across roughly 0.95 hectares.
